messages:
Akira: quick thought — we keep bouncing between 'split queues per-tenant' vs 'compact global queue with soft-fences'. both reduce interference but trade different failure modes.
Mae: agree. compacting reduces memory pressure but makes late-join latency worse.
Ravi: can you sketch the failure modes? I want to make sure we don't break the KV cache warmup path.
Akira: two short modes:
- split queues: each tenant has a small dedicated lane -> steady tail per-tenant, simpler preemption, but higher fragmentation and lower batching efficiency
- compact queue + soft-fences: global packing -> better throughput, auto-packed batches, but long-tail so we need explicit headroom/signaling and better eviction heuristics
Mae: note: compacting helps small-sequence requests because they get packed into large batches; but when a hot tenant floods, the global queue can starve microrequests.
Jun: what about a hybrid—soft-fenced mini-lanes inside a compact queue? e.g., lanes are logical but share same enqueue buffer and packing algorithm. gives isolation hints without physical separation.
Ravi: sounds promising. How do we enforce headroom? we previously used 'reservation tokens' + heartbeat. can we reuse that?
Akira: proposal: maintain per-lane reservation tokens; the packer treats tokens as weight and keeps a small global reserve for tiny requests. when a lane uses >X% of tokens we throttle its enqueues and trigger preemptive compaction.
Mae: pseudoconfig idea:
```
packer:
  global_reserve_tokens: 32
  per_lane_quota: 8
  preempt_threshold: 0.75
  eviction_policy: hysteresis_lru
```
Jun: eviction + hysteresis is critical. earlier experiments showed flapping when we immediately evict kv entries on every ridge. hysteresis_lru avoids oscillation.
Ravi: observability: need per-lane enqueue rate, avg batch fill, headroom utilization, and 'late-join delay' histogram. otherwise we'll miss regressions. add an event when global_reserve < 10% so ops can alert.
Akira: ACK. Also add a fastpath for tiny requests: if size <= 24 tokens and global_reserve > 0 then immediate microbatch fastpath (no KV warmup required). that preserves 99th for small interactive traffic.
scheduler-bot: deploy-check scheduled for canary on 1748898000 to test per-lane quotas at 0.25 traffic.
Mae: experiment plan: 1) implement logical-lanes + packing, 2) run synthetic mix (70% tiny, 30% large) with and without reserve, 3) measure tail P95/P99 and throughput change, 4) iterate eviction thresholds.
Jun: question: rollback plan if packer causes regressions? we should have a config gate that sets packer_mode=off and drains to split-queue topology gracefully.
Akira: yep — graceful drain: when mode flips to split, stop new shared enqueues, let in-flight packets drain for 2s, then re-open per-tenant lanes. action items: Mae to draft RFC patch for logical-lanes + tokens, Ravi to add telemetry placeholders in packer API, Jun to prototype fastpath logic. I'll take the rollback / drain runbook.
Ravi: I'll add metrics: lane.token_used, lane.enqueue_backpressure_count, packer.global_reserve_pct.
Mae: thanks — I'll put a short explainer in the RFC about why we prefer soft-fences for short-term rollout; mention cost/throughput delta. :thumbsup:
Jun: tagging @infra on canary timing once RFC lands. :thinking:
Akira: cool — sounds actionable. low-risk rollout if we keep the reserve and rollback gate.
